subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw define a core owner-confirmed responsibility-state contract for memory, reusable evidence, skill outputs, and action authorization, or split this umbrella into narrower existing provenance and approval issues first?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses durable memory storage, retrieval policy, plugin SDK/API surface, security boundaries, UI audit state, and config defaults, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Keep umbrella, design first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella until maintainers define the responsibility states and then cut narrow implementation issues for memory/evidence, skill outputs, and action gates.

options.title: Split to existing canonical issues
options.body: Move the remaining work into the narrower memory trust, persistent provenance, and source-aware execution issues, then close this only after the mapping is explicit.

options.title: External integration only
options.body: Treat SCBKR/UMP as optional plugin or ClawHub interoperability work, but this leaves the missing core memory/evidence lifecycle unresolved unless maintainers explicitly reject core support.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella, design first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella until maintainers define the responsibility states and then cut narrow implementation issues for memory/evidence, skill outputs, and action gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The highest-confidence history trail for the durable memory boundary points to Peter Steinberger's memory host and memory-core refactors.
